title: Review: all 22 letters
topic: review of the whole alef-bet, the final letters, and the dagesh
why: Review of the alef-bet: the 22 letters, the five final forms, the dagesh and the letters that sound the same, with new words made only of letters you know. We finish with יֵשׁ / אֵין to say what you have, enough to introduce yourself before the next unit.

Traps to avoid

Letters that look alike: ב / כ (the bet has a little foot at the bottom right), ד / ר (corner or rounded), ה / ח (left leg detached or attached), ו / ז / ן, ס / ם.

SoundLettersExample
tת טתְּמוּנָה, טוֹב
kכּ קכֶּלֶב, קָר
khכ ך חמֶלֶךְ, לֶחֶם
vב ועֶרֶב, דָּוִד
sס שׂסוּס, שָׂמֵחַ
silentא עאֶרֶץ, עֵץ

The dagesh changes the sound of only three letters: בּ / ב, כּ / כ, פּ / פ. The five final forms ך ם ן ף ץ are only used at the end of a word.

For a new word, always do the same thing: letter by letter, from right to left, each letter with its vowel. צִ־פּוֹר → tsi-por, a bird.

יֵשׁ and אֵין: there is, I have

יֵשׁ (yesh) means \"there is / there are\"; אֵין (ein), \"there isn't / there aren't\". With לִי (to me), it gives \"I have\": יֵשׁ לִי, literally \"there is to me\".

יֵשׁ לִי אָח וְאָחוֹת.I have a brother and a sister. [yesh li akh ve-akhot]
אֵין לִי כֶּלֶב.I don't have a dog. [ein li kelev]
יֵשׁ לְךָ חָתוּל? / יֵשׁ לָךְ חָתוּל?Do you have a cat? (to a man / to a woman) [yesh lekha khatul? / yesh lakh khatul?]

To introduce someone: זֶה אִיתַי (this is Itai), זֹאת נֹעָה (this is Noa).

Hebrew has no word for \"a\", and nothing like \"any\" after the negative: אֵין לִי כֶּלֶב, literally \"there isn't to me dog\".
